proposals.entity_key: Adjectives change meaning based on position
value: The adjective still agrees in gender and number with the noun, whatever its position
Position affects meaning only, never agreement

evidence.notes: Standard agreement behaviour for adjectives; the rule itself concerns meaning, not agreement.

value: No past participle agreement arises; the added form is a stressed pronoun, not a participle
The pronoun form depends on the subject (toi, nous, vous) but never on gender

evidence.notes: Derived from the stated formation (verb + stressed pronoun).

value: The past participle agrees with the subject, as in all passive constructions
The agent introduced by de does not affect agreement

evidence.notes: Standard passive agreement; the rule only concerns the choice of preposition.

value: The past participle agrees with the subject, never with the agent
The agent introduced by par never triggers agreement
In compound tenses the past participle agrees in gender and number with the subject (elle est allée)
The destination phrase after à triggers no agreement

evidence.notes: Standard agreement for aller with être; the rule itself covers preposition contraction.

value: In compound tenses the past participle agrees with the subject (elle est allée)

value: With être as auxiliary, the past participle of the past conditional agrees with the subject

proposals.entity_key: Avoir and être are irregular in the passé simple
value: The passé simple agrees in person and number with the subject (eus/fus, eûmes/fûmes)
The passé simple has no participle and therefore no gender agreement

evidence.notes: Derived from the given conjugation tables; the rule itself concerns irregular stems.
